source: កូនសៀវភៅ ស្តីពី ផលិតកម្មដំណាំស្រូវពង្រោះដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ (Climate Resilient Broadcasting Rice Growing Technique), ASPIRE/IFAD, MAFF, Feb 2018
text: Choosing a rice variety (ការជ្រើសរើសពូជ) for broadcasting starts with a few practical criteria: high yield with good aroma, pure seed with high germination (above 85%), a maturity length that fits the planting window, tolerance to drought and to the pests/diseases common in the area, and good milling/eating quality. Varieties fall into three duration groups by days-to-maturity: short-duration (roughly 90-110 days), medium-duration, and long/heavy-duration (photoperiod-sensitive types that only flower once a year regardless of planting date). Varieties also split into two groups by day-length sensitivity: photoperiod-insensitive varieties can be sown in any season (dry season, early wet season, or late wet season) with only small shifts in maturity length, while photoperiod-sensitive varieties flower on a fixed calendar date no matter when they were sown, so they can only be grown once per year timed to that flowering window. A further split is by aroma: aromatic varieties (both grain and cooked rice have a distinct fragrance) versus non-aromatic varieties. Farmers should ask what duration group and sensitivity type a variety belongs to before deciding when to sow it, rather than assuming any variety can be planted at any time of year.
